title: control-plane.gate-decision.v1 event body
description: A human release-gate decision, relayed onto the bus. The status vocabulary below is exactly what the consumer accepts; anything else is rejected as unusable, so it is written down here rather than left to be discovered by a rejected message.

metrics.description: Carries nothing for this topic. A decision is not a measurement.

payload.description: Exactly one of 'decision' or 'status' must carry the verdict. The consumer reads decision first and falls back to status, so a message with neither has no usable verdict and is rejected.

decided_by.description: An identity on the wire - typically a username. Distinct from the consumer's internal provenance field of the same name, which records only whether a human or a replayed fixture resolved the gate.

clarified_requirement.description: Absent and null are not the same thing: the consumer only applies this key when it is actually supplied, because a present-but-null value would erase the current requirement.

verdict.description: 'approve'/'reject' are normalised by the consumer to 'approved'/'rejected'. Both spellings are on the wire and both are accepted.
